title: Machine scrubbing and drying with a wet suction machine
audience: Trained cleaning operative who will run a battery-powered scrubber-drier with a wet suction head on hard floors, under supervision.
learningOutcomes: Complete the before-use checks on a wet suction scrubber, including electrical status, pad condition and fluid levels.
Select the pad and fluid flow setting for the surface being cleaned and explain why each matters.
Move the machine at a steady speed and monitor the floor during the pass so the scrub and dry result is achieved.
Carry out end-of-use checks, empty and clean the waste tank, and store the machine safely on charge or upright.

instruction.heading: What this machine does and where the risks sit
instruction.body: A wet suction scrubber applies cleaning solution to the floor through a brush or pad, scrubs the surface, and then pulls the dirty liquid back into a waste tank. It is a battery-powered electrical machine with rotating parts, a fluid circuit, a charging point and a heavy body. The main risks are electrical faults, a fall or slip on wet floor, chemical contact and fumes, and damage to the floor finish or to the machine if the pad, fluid flow or speed is wrong. The procedure set out here is written for trained operators. Completing this lesson does not qualify you to operate the machine on a site.

instruction.heading: Before-use checks
instruction.body: Before the machine is used, confirm that it is unplugged from its charging source. Check the electrical safety test date against the site register, and look over the plug and lead for damage, bare wires or tape repairs. Inspect every part of the machine for obvious damage, including the body, the anti-splash skirt, the wheels and the brush or pad holder. Condition the machine and check that every fluid level is correct for the job. Select the brush or pad that suits the surface. Secure the anti-splash skirt. Check that the battery holds enough charge to finish the area. Switch the machine on, then set the fluid flow to the level the job requires.

instruction.heading: Selecting pads and fluid flow
instruction.body: Pads are colour coded by abrasiveness. A darker pad is more abrasive, so choose the lightest pad that will do the job for the surface and the soil. Too much fluid leaves the floor slippery and wastes solution, while too little leaves the surface under-cleaned. Match the flow to the surface and adjust it during the job if the floor is drying too fast or leaving a film. Chemicals must be labelled and must be washed out of the equipment before a different product is used, so that two products are never mixed by accident.

instruction.heading: Running the machine
instruction.body: Move the machine across the floor at a steady pace that gives the scrub and suction time to work. Going too fast leaves the surface dirty, and going too slowly can over-wet the floor or damage the finish. Watch the floor as you work and check the result on each pass, not just at the end. Keep ventilation open where possible, because fumes from cleaning products are harmful and air movement helps the floor dry faster. Keep the machine under control at all times and never leave it running unattended. Keep electrical checks in mind throughout: stop immediately if the machine behaves unusually, the lead is pinched, or the floor is too wet to work on safely.

instruction.heading: End-of-use checks
instruction.body: After use, complete the listed checks to confirm that the machine has not been damaged during the job. Empty the waste fluid tank and remove any residue from inside it, following the site's waste disposal procedure. Remove the brush or pad, safety check and damp wipe the machine, and wash the pad and let it dry. Put the machine on charge if it needs it, using the charging point, and store it upright. Never store the machine with a pad or brush still fitted.

instruction.heading: Recording the job
instruction.body: Record the before-use check, the fluid settings used, the area covered, the end-of-use check and the disposal of the waste. A faulty machine, a missed test, or a damaged part must be reported and tagged out before the next use. Recording the checks is what shows the machine was safe and the work was done to standard, not the time spent on the floor.

procedure: Confirm the machine is unplugged from its charging source and that the approved pad and solution are on the job sheet.
Check the electrical safety test date and inspect the plug and lead. Tag out the machine if any fault is found.
Inspect the body, anti-splash skirt, wheels and pad holder for visible damage.
Condition the machine and check all fluid levels against the job requirement.
Select the brush or pad suited to the surface and fit it securely.
Secure the anti-splash skirt and check battery charge for the area.
Switch the machine on and set the fluid flow for the surface.
Move at a steady speed, keeping the scrub and suction working, and check the floor on each pass.
Keep ventilation open, stay alert for faults, and never leave the machine running unattended.
Stop, switch off and report any unusual behaviour, pinched lead or unsafe floor condition.
After use, empty the waste tank, remove residue, and dispose of waste per the site procedure.
Remove the brush or pad, safety check and damp wipe the machine, wash and dry the pad.
Charge the machine if needed and store it upright with no pad fitted.

workedExamples.situation: A trained operator starts a wet suction scrub on a hard floor in a shared lobby. The machine's lead has been repaired with tape near the plug, and the pad is worn on one side.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What does the operator do before starting the scrub?
workedExamples.reasoning: The taped lead fails the before-use check. The machine must not be used, and it should be tagged out and reported. The worn pad is also a fault: it will not scrub evenly. Replace the pad only if a suitable one is available, otherwise report it. Starting the job with either fault breaks the check, however long the job would take.

workedExamples.situation: Halfway through a scrub, the floor starts to look shiny and slightly slippery in one corner, and the operator notices the machine is leaving a thin film.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What is the most likely cause and the correct response?
workedExamples.reasoning: Too much solution is being applied, or the solution is being left to dry rather than suctioned. Reduce the fluid flow, check that the squeegee and suction are working, and recheck the pass. Keep the floor safe for pedestrians by barriering the wet area while it dries.

equipmentAndPpe: Battery-powered wet suction scrubber-drier with charging point
Colour-coded brushes or pads suited to the surface
Anti-splash skirt, squeegee and waste tank
Wet floor warning signs and barriers
Gloves and eye protection suited to the product
Ventilation: doors and windows opened where possible
Waste disposal bags or containers as the site requires

commonErrors.error: Starting the machine without completing the electrical and pad checks.
commonErrors.prevention: Work through the before-use checklist in order every time, and tag out any machine that fails it.

commonErrors.error: Setting the fluid flow too high, leaving the floor wet and slippery.
commonErrors.prevention: Match fluid flow to the surface, adjust during the job, and barrier the wet area until it dries.

commonErrors.error: Storing the machine with the brush or pad still fitted, or charging it with a damaged pad.
commonErrors.prevention: Remove the pad, safety check and wash it, then store the machine upright and charge it as the procedure states.

commonErrors.error: Leaving dirty waste in the tank after the job.
commonErrors.prevention: Empty and clean the tank at the end of every job, and dispose of waste according to the site procedure.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Only trained operators use this machine. Operator training is required before use. Completing this lesson does not certify you to operate the equipment or any similar machine.
Electrical equipment must be tested and tagged, or inspected, under the local rule, with the register kept up to date. The source names PAT testing.
Chemicals must be used as their label directs and the safety data sheet is available on site.
Stop and tag out the machine if the lead, plug, pad holder or battery shows damage, or if the machine behaves unexpectedly while in use.

qualityStandard: The floor is scrubbed across the full area with no missed lines or unclean bands.
The floor dries without film, streaks or standing water in the work area.
Fluid flow matched the surface for the whole job and the check was recorded.
The waste tank is emptied and cleaned, and the pad is washed and dried.
The machine is stored upright, with no pad fitted, and is on charge if required.
documentationEvidence: Before-use check record, with electrical test status and any fault found
Pad colour and cleaning solution used for each area, with label reference
Area covered and time on task
End-of-use check, including waste disposal method
Any fault, damage or near miss reported to the supervisor
summary: Before use, check the electrical test status, the lead, the body, the pad and the fluid levels.
Choose the pad and fluid flow for the surface, and keep the machine moving at a steady speed.
After use, empty and clean the waste tank, safety check the machine, and store it upright with no pad fitted.
Report and tag out any fault. Operators must be trained before they run the machine.

knowledgeChecks.question: Before a wet suction scrubber is used, which check does the procedure require?
options: Only that the battery is fully charged, and the water tank and the squeegee are in place before you start
The electrical test status, the condition of the plug and lead, and an inspection of every part of the machine
Only that the pad is the correct colour for the job and that the pad is fitted tightly to the machine before use
That another operator has used the machine on the same site the day before and reported no faults

knowledgeChecks.question: What should happen to the waste fluid tank at the end of a scrubbing job?
options: It is left full so the next operator can see how much was collected
It is emptied and any residue is removed from inside
It is topped up with clean water so it is ready for the next job
It is sealed and left attached to the machine until the next visit

knowledgeChecks.question: How should the scrubber be stored after use?
options: Lying on its side with the pad fitted to keep the shape of the pad
Upright, with the pad and base plate removed, and put on charge if needed
Upright, with the pad fitted so it is ready for the next job
Stacked on top of another machine to save floor space
